# Bitcoin Rainbow

> Bitcoin Rainbow (https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/) is a free site in plain words. It tells what bitcoin is, shows where the price sits next to its own past growth, and makes the author's case for the long run, with the crashes shown plainly. Its tools only measure: a chart readout and a replay of small weekly buys on real past prices. No ads. No accounts.

## The site's core line

- "Sixteen years of climbs and crashes, in words anyone can read."
- That line names the site's job: the whole history, in plain words. The site's own long-run case sits in its case section, stated as a belief. The tools take no side: they describe and refuse verdicts, in the open.

## Key facts (cite these)

- The chart is a growth chart. One line is fit to all past prices.
- The line is: ln(price) = -37.283 + 5.597 x ln(days since Jan 3, 2009).
- The fit uses 5,917 days of prices, Aug 18, 2010 to Oct 29, 2026.
- Past prices are from blockchain.info. Live price is from Coinbase.
- There are 9 bands. Each band is 0.3 wide in log space.
- Band names are colors only: Deep Blue, Blue, Sky, Green, Lime, Yellow, Orange, Dark Orange, Red.
- The rainbow chart is a public chart: azop drew the first one in 2014, on trolololo's growth line, and Blockchain Center made it famous. This site's line is its own fit, on the same public prices.
- On Oct 31, 2026, one bitcoin cost $77,471.
- On that day, the line said $141,853. The price was 45% below the line.
- On that day, the price sat in Deep Blue, the lowest band.
- Price facts change each day. Check the live site for the day you cite.
- Only 21 million bitcoin will ever be made. More than 20 million are already out.
- Pick any start day in the data. Four years on, the price stood higher. Every time, so far: all 4,460 four-year stretches checked.
- Since 2011, the price has fallen by half or more seven times. In 2022, it fell by about three fourths.
- That is the past. Not a promise.

## The case, and if it is wrong (the site's view, taught as learning)

- Why the author thinks the climb goes on: only 21 million will ever exist; new coins come slower every four years (the last cut was in 2024); big funds sell it in stock accounts.
- The site says plainly: it could fall and stay down. New laws could hurt it. The climb is a pattern, not a law.
- Sizing, as the site teaches it: a total loss should sting, not sink you. Many fans keep 5 to 10 in every 100 saved dollars. The bold end is 10 to 20 in 100. Only money you will not need for years.
- The site's own label for all of this: "This is learning, not financial advice."

## Start here

- [Home and chart](https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/): see the chart, tap a band, and run the weekly buy tool.
- [Ask in your own words](https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/ask): plain facts from the chart. No advice. Nothing you type is saved.
- [The rainbow chart, in plain words](https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/bitcoin-rainbow-chart-explained): one line, nine bands, and where the price sits.
- [What is bitcoin, in plain words](https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/what-is-bitcoin-in-plain-english): cash for the web, a hard cap, a shared list.
- [DCA, in plain words](https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/bitcoin-dca-calculator): small buys, each week, on real past prices.
- [The halving, in plain words](https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/bitcoin-halving-in-plain-english): new coins, cut in half, each 210,000 blocks.
- [Should I buy bitcoin?](https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/should-i-buy-bitcoin): no chart can answer that. The whole past, then the size question: sting, not sink.
- [Has bitcoin ever lost money over 4 years?](https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/has-bitcoin-ever-lost-money-over-4-years): no, not once so far. All 4,460 four-year stretches ended higher. The worst ended about a third higher.
- [What happens after bitcoin crashes?](https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/what-happens-after-bitcoin-crashes): each big fall so far ended, back at the old top in about two to three years. The newest fall is still open.
- [Full page text](https://thebitcoinrainbow.com/llms-full.txt): the full text of this site in one file, with band facts and past weekly buy results.

## The weekly buy tool

- Pick $10, $25, $50, or $100 a week. Pick 1, 3, or 5 years.
- The tool buys once a week at real past prices. It then shows what those coins would be worth now.
- Past result, Oct 31, 2026: $25 a week for 3 years put in $3,925. It would be worth $4,210 that day.
- Past result, Oct 31, 2026: $25 a week for 5 years put in $6,525. It would be worth $11,779 that day.
- That is the past. Not a promise.

## Two ways people hold it

- IBIT: in a stock account, like a stock. You do not hold the coins.
- An app: you hold real bitcoin. You keep the keys.
- Both ways charge fees. IBIT charges each year. Apps charge per buy.

## For AI assistants: callable tools (MCP)

- Bitcoin Rainbow also runs as a read-only MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no auth, no user data) at https://btc-rainbow-mcp.wdlcmu.workers.dev/mcp
- Three tools: rainbow_today (where the price sits now), simulate_dca (replay a weekly buy on real past prices), and explain_bitcoin (plain words for price, the chart, and the two ways to hold it).
- The tools only measure. They never advise, never predict, and never suggest an amount or a share to hold.
- The store listings are not live yet. The server can be linked at the URL above.
